name: East Wenatchee
deadline_pattern: No fixed cycle. Tourism Promotion Grant applications are accepted year-round and must be submitted at least 60 days before the event; EWEB reviews them at its monthly meeting (first Wednesday, 3:00 pm) and forwards recommendations to City Council
typical_open: Open year-round; apply at least 60 days ahead of the event
annual_pool: Not published. EWEB page gives no fund total or award caps; Wenatchee World (undated) reported council approving three previously tabled lodging tax requests without amounts
contact: East Wenatchee Events Board (EWEB) / Events Department, 271 9th Street NE, East Wenatchee, WA 98802, 509-886-6108 (EWEB line); City Hall 509-884-9515; staff name not published on the EWEB page (an Events Director was hired in 2019)
notes: The lodging tax advisory committee here is the East Wenatchee Events Board (EWEB), a 5 to 7 member council-appointed board that doubles as the city's events board. Applicants complete the Tourism Promotion Grant Application, give a 3 to 5 minute presentation at a monthly EWEB meeting, and if approved by EWEB and then City Council sign a contract; payment is reimbursement within 30 days of a post-event report and invoice, which are due within 30 days after the event. Funding is for tourism marketing, special events and festivals, and tourism facilities under RCW 67.28.1816. The Tourism Promotion Grant program page could not be fetched directly.

presentation.pattern: Applicant presents at the next monthly EWEB meeting after submitting (first Wednesday of the month, 3:00 pm); upcoming meetings Nov 4 and Dec 2, 2026
presentation.format: 3 to 5 minute in-person presentation followed by questions from the board, at Eastmont Parks and Recreation Community Center, 230 N Georgia Ave

meeting_schedule: First Wednesday of each month at 3:00 pm, Eastmont Parks and Recreation Community Center, 230 N Georgia Avenue, East Wenatchee; agendas posted the Friday before
pool_note: No fund total, budget line or award list is published on the EWEB or grant pages; the city's budget document was not located. Because applications are rolling, the open pool is whatever remains in the Hotel/Motel Tax fund for the year.

name: Monroe
deadline_pattern: Applications open early October and close the first Monday of November at 5:00 pm for the following calendar year (Oct 5 to Nov 2, 2026 for 2027; Oct 9, 2024 deadline for 2025). Postmarks not accepted
annual_pool: 2026 awards totaled $115,000 across 14 projects (largest: Chamber Visitor Information Center $65,000); 2027 pool not published
contact: Liam McKorkle, Management Analyst (LTAC staff liaison), lmckorkle@monroewa.gov, 360-322-0852; Ben Warthan, Interim City Administrator, bwarthan@monroewa.gov, 360-863-4500; City Hall 806 W Main St, Monroe, WA 98272
notes: Applications are scored on six criteria (organizational capacity, innovation, marketing, collaboration, visitor economic impact, overnight-stay economic impact) plus up to six bonus points, with priority for November to April off-season events. Grants are reimbursement only after a municipal services contract is signed; awardees attend a January webinar. Historically the Chamber's visitor center takes more than half the pool, leaving roughly $50,000 for events in 2026. Two of the five LTAC seats were vacant as of Oct 2026.

pool_note: 2026: $115,000 awarded in total (sum of the posted award list). $65,000 went to the Chamber of Commerce Visitor Information Center and $6,300 to City of Monroe line items (restrooms, digital marketing, Cascade Loop), leaving about $43,700 for outside event and marketing grants; the Chamber also received $15,700 for two events. Rounded competitive figure of $50,000 treats the Chamber's event grants as competitive.
